key_insight: Fixed schema graphs are not required for strong relational deep learning; learning full-resolution graph structure (including instance- and schema-level edges) end-to-end with GNNs yields better, more robust relational prediction than relying on a manually fixed schema graph.
problem_solved: Eliminates dependence on a single hand-crafted/fixed schema graph for relational databases, addressing brittle or incomplete graph constructions that hurt downstream relational prediction.
method: Formulate graph structure learning at full resolution: allow the model to add, remove, or reweight edges at both schema and instance levels rather than fixing schema topology.
Jointly learn graph structure and GNN parameters end-to-end so relational semantics are preserved while optimizing prediction performance.
Use learned edge scores/attention and regularization to keep structure interpretable and stable, enabling transfer across tables and noisy schemas.
impact: Automates and improves graph construction for RDB-based ML workflows, reducing manual schema engineering and improving accuracy and robustness for practitioners using GNNs on relational data.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: fixed schema graph vs. learned full-resolution graph, highlighting added/removed edges
Pipeline schematic: RDB → graph-structure learner (edge scoring) → GNN → prediction
Performance chart: accuracy/ROC comparison between fixed-schema baseline and learned-structure model across several tasks
Edge-importance heatmap or attention visualization over a sample database showing which relations are learned/strengthened
paper_title: Is Fixing Schema Graphs Necessary? Full-Resolution Graph Structure Learning for Relational Deep Learning
paper_authors: Yi Huang, Qingyun Sun, Jia Li, Xingcheng Fu, Jianxin Li
